text:
jordan: Rough brain-dump: propose a "safety lattice" runway for canary/A-B rollouts + automated fallback. Goal: predictable, tenant-respectful degradation that avoids cascade. Need quick feedback before putting together RFC.

mei: can you sketch the core pieces? high level bullets ok.

jordan: sure. bullets: 1) multi-signal vector (latency p95, errors, quality-samples, queue-depth), 2) discretize into named "cells", 3) cells map to ordered mitigation steps (divert, variant-pin, lower-qos, full fallback), 4) each step has preconds + revert + cooldown.

samir: how is this different from our current decision plane? seems similar to decision tables.
jordan: key diffs: (a) cells are partial-ordered (a lattice) so we can combine signals compositionally, (b) every cell carries a cost/severity weight for multi-tenant prioritization, (c) ephemeral central eval that emits signed decision tokens to edges.

elena: concern: state explosion if we combine many signals. what's the bounding strategy?
jordan: two levers: bucket coarsening (percentile buckets, not raw values) and cardinality cap with LRU-like eviction for rare combos. Also we only materialize cells that are hit in last N minutes.

mei: neat. what about false positives? e.g., a noisy p95 spike.
jordan: mitigation layers: signal smoothing + outlier suppression + action preconditions (e.g., only divert if model QPS > threshold) + min dwell time before action. plus a verification probe after an action to check quality signal.

samir: verification probe sounds important. do you mean synthetic prompts?
jordan: yes. spawn a small targeted probe job that runs representative prompts against the fallback target and primary. If quality gap is below threshold, auto-revert.

elena: where do we evaluate the cell membership? centrally or at edge?
jordan: central evaluator consumes aggregated metrics, keeps the lattice aggregates, decides cell transitions, then publishes tokens. Edge subscribes, applies diffs. Local caches avoid hotpath evals at edge.

mei: tokens need to be compact and secure. include version + TTL + origin signature?\ordan: (typo) jordan: yes include version, TTL, signature, and provenance blob (small). Tokens should be cheap to validate.

samir: policy config — who writes the cell->action mapping? product or infra?
jordan: infra ships action primitives (templates + safety knobs). Product teams author per-product policy manifests referencing templates. Tenant-level overrides allowed but gated by a safety policy.

elena: audit & explainability are critical. ops needs to know which signal and threshold fired an action.
jordan: every decision token contains trace_id and the triggering signal vector. We'll sample detailed traces and store diffs for the UI.

ops-bot: alert: canary deployment shadow-x deployed to release-zone-7 at 2026-03-15T12:40:00Z

mei: performance: are we putting policy evals on the ingestion path? that's risky.
jordan: central evaluator is downstream of ingestion (eventual). We optimize by pre-aggregating via our existing observer-runner and using in-memory windows. No blocking writes.

samir: rollout choreography: soft-fail budgets per tenant sound useful. e.g., we degrade lower-tier tenants first.
jordan: yep. cells include tenant-priority weighting and budget checks before applying global-impact actions. We also allow an "escape hatch" manual override in the console.

elena: want a rehearsal mode: run lattice decisions in dry-run against historical telemetry to estimate false positive rate.
jordan: agreed — simulate configs against historical traces before making them active. Add a CI step to policy changes.

mei: DSL for conditions — needs percentile ops, time-window operators, and cross-signal expressions. probably a small expression language with safe eval.
jordan: propose: condition DSL -> compiled to bytecode for fast eval in central component. We'll version the DSL.
samir: testing: add unit + integration + chaos tests and a small simulator that can fuzz signals to find unstable configs.
jordan: noted. I'll include simulation harness + replay in RFC.

elena: ops UX: timeline view, reversible diffs, and a gentle notification channel for affected owners.
jordan: console will show timeline + action provenance + links to logs and probe results. Also slack/ops autopings for major fallbacks.

ops-bot: runbook updated: 'fallback-manual-override' patched by elena at 2026-03-15T12:50:02Z

mei: ok great. next steps?
jordan: I'll draft RFC with: data model, token schema, action primitives, condition DSL, ownership model, simulation plan, and ops UX. Want review from infra + product.

samir: please include the simulation metrics we should gate on.
jordan: will do. ping me when draft ready. :thumbsup:
